Body:
Light from free space is incident at an angle $\scriptstyle \theta_i$ to the normal of the facet of a step-index large core optical fibre. The core and cladding refractive indices are $\scriptstyle n_1=1.5$ and $\scriptstyle n_2=1.4$, respectively.

The maximum value of $\scriptstyle \theta_i$ (in degrees) for which the incident light will be guided in the core of the fibre is ________
Explanation:
Given: free-space index $\scriptstyle n_0=1$, core index $\scriptstyle n_1=1.5$, cladding index $\scriptstyle n_2=1.4$.
Concept: light stays guided only when it undergoes total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary. Let $\scriptstyle \theta_r$ be the refraction angle inside the core at the fibre facet. The ray then meets the core-cladding boundary at an angle of incidence $\scriptstyle 90^{\circ}-\theta_r$.
Refraction at the facet (Snell's law): $\scriptstyle \sin\theta_i=n_1\sin\theta_r$.
Limiting case of total internal reflection: $\scriptstyle \sin(90^{\circ}-\theta_r)=\cos\theta_r=\tfrac{n_2}{n_1}$.
Then $\scriptstyle \sin\theta_r=\sqrt{1-\left(\tfrac{n_2}{n_1}\right)^2}=\tfrac{\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}}{n_1}$.
Substituting in Snell's law: $\scriptstyle \sin\theta_{i,max}=n_1\sin\theta_r=\sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}=\sqrt{1.5^2-1.4^2}=\sqrt{0.29}=0.5385$.
So $\scriptstyle \theta_{i,max}=\sin^{-1}(0.5385)\approx 32.6^{\circ}$.
Hence the maximum angle of incidence is about $\scriptstyle 32.6^{\circ}$.

Tip: For a ray coming from free space, the core index cancels out and only $\scriptstyle \sqrt{n_1^2-n_2^2}=\sqrt{0.29}$ matters (the numerical aperture of this fibre), so any larger angle than this lets the ray hit the cladding below the critical angle and leak out.
Subject: EMFT - ECE
Topic: Plane Waves (Normal and Oblique incidence of Plane Waves)
